title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
authors: Daan Holleman, Luuk Klein Nagelvoort, Monica Morales-Masis, Linn Leppert
abstract: Metal-halide perovskites are promising photovoltaic absorbers whose optoelectronic properties are highly tunable. Epitaxial strain offers a route to stabilize desirable phases, tune band gaps, and reduce energetic disorder, but rational strain engineering requires predictive models. Static, zero-temperature "strained-bulk" density functional theory (DFT) calculations, successful for oxide perovskites, neglect the dynamic disorder and anharmonicity that govern halide perovskites at ambient temperature. Here, we show that molecular dynamics (MD) based on machine-learned force fields trained on-the-fly on DFT reproduces the structural and optoelectronic response of methylammonium (MA) lead iodide (MAPbI$_3$) to epitaxial strain at 300 K. We simulate bulk and free-standing slab models across experimentally accessible biaxial strains by locking the in-plane lattice vectors in nanosecond-long simulations. We predict a tetragonal-to-cubic transition at $\sim$0.5% tensile strain, marked by $c/a = 1$ and the loss of the $a^0a^0c^-$ tilting pattern, in agreement with experiments on epitaxial MAPbI$_3$ films on KCl. MA cations retain preferential orientations in the strain-induced cubic phase, unlike in its temperature-induced counterpart. Bulk and slab models yield consistent trends, with surface effects decaying within a few octahedral layers. Band gaps computed as ensemble averages over MD snapshots blue-shift under tensile strain, consistent with experiment, whereas static calculations on averaged structures predict a red shift. Our study positions MD with constrained lattice vectors as a method for predicting finite-temperature strain phase diagrams and guiding the epitaxial design of perovskite absorbers.

infographic.key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that about 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while increasing its band gap.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial design of perovskite solar absorbers where static calculations miss dynamic structural and electronic responses.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track lattice symmetry, octahedral tilts, molecular orientations, and snapshot-averaged band gaps.
infographic.evidence_signal: The predicted transition and tensile-strain band-gap blue shift agree with reported experiments, while bulk and slab models show consistent trends.
infographic.watch_item: Predictions concern MAPbI₃ at 300 K; applicability to other compositions, temperatures, or explicit substrate interfaces requires validation.
infographic.paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics

title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
authors: YanKai Chen, Zhi Wan, ZiHao Li, Tao Jing
abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,035 training articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their initial efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 $^\circ$C. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

infographic.key_insight: Training language models on evidence-linked scientific reasoning helped guide perovskite solar-cell design, with a model-selected contact enabling 27.05% power conversion efficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evidence-grounded AI could help engineers prioritize contact materials and design discriminating experiments for more efficient, thermally stable perovskite devices.
method: Reconstruct expert-calibrated evidence records from 4,035 articles, linking strategies, controls and observations to mechanisms.
Adapt OpenPerov using structured evidence rather than conventional question-answer training.
Refine selected answers with retrieved evidence and experimentally test a recommended self-assembled monolayer contact.
infographic.evidence_signal: On the 800-question PSM-Bench, OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems; experimentally, the model-selected K analogue outperformed the expert-preferred Na analogue, with devices retaining 96.74% efficiency after 1,000 hours of dark thermal ageing at 85°C.
infographic.watch_item: The reported validation does not establish generalization across other material systems or durability under illuminated operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization

title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
authors: Zixu Huang, Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, David S. Ginger
abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite solar cells occurs preferentially at the HTL interface, adversely affecting device stability, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests. Our results also show that modifying the buried interface with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces UV-induced damage at the buried interface, thus improving the UV stability of both perovskite films and devices. This work establishes a fast, non-destructive strategy to screen depth-dependent degradation in perovskite devices, offering insights for interface design and stability optimization.

infographic.key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, locating preferential degradation at the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface UV damage and improving stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence excitation.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements during UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n devices with different indium tin oxide surface modifiers.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements identified preferential buried-interface degradation consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, while interface modification improved UV stability in both films and devices.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains, and validation beyond UV soaking remains necessary.
infographic.paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors

title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
authors: Ashraful Mamun, Andrew Allison, Meng-Jen, Wang, Etee Kawna Roy, Edward Cazalas
abstract: Thin-film CdTe solar cells are promising candidates for lightweight space power, but device-level studies of their response to neutron irradiation remain scarce. Here, we report the device performance of CdS/CdTe solar cells irradiated for 10 to 150 min in the thermal irradiator of a TRIGA reactor (90 kW), corresponding to nominal total neutron fluences of 3.3 x 10^14 to 5.0 x 10^15 n cm-2. The cells were characterized after 18 months of post-irradiation storage, once the residual activity has decayed to background levels. Co-irradiated FTO-coated glass reference substrates exhibit a wavelength-dependent transmission loss, with the transmittance at 500 nm decreasing from 80 % to 50 % after 60 min of irradiation. The irradiated cells retain rectifying behavior, but the reverse-bias dark current, photocurrent, and efficiency generally decrease with exposure time. Post-irradiation annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination initially improves Jsc and Voc, with the highest efficiency after 4 h. Prolonged annealing, however, causes substantial FF degradation despite continued photocurrent recovery. These trends suggest that irradiation-induced changes in the glass substrate, CdTe absorber, and contacts respond differently to annealing. Understanding underlying defect chemistry and correlating it with device behavior are necessary steps toward radiation-tolerant CdTe photovoltaics for space applications.

infographic.key_insight: Neutron-irradiated CdS/CdTe solar cells show persistent performance losses after 18 months, with partial recovery during short annealing but fill-factor degradation during prolonged treatment.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Radiation-tolerant CdTe space photovoltaics require coordinated optimization of substrates, absorbers, contacts, and recovery treatments.
method: Irradiate cells for 10–150 min in a 90 kW TRIGA reactor at nominal neutron fluences of 3.3 × 10^14–5.0 × 10^15 n/cm².
Characterize device performance and co-irradiated FTO-coated glass after 18 months of storage.
Evaluate recovery by annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination.
infographic.evidence_signal: FTO-coated glass transmission at 500 nm fell from 80% to 50% after 60 min of irradiation; annealed cells reached their highest efficiency after 4 h.
infographic.watch_item: Defect mechanisms remain unresolved, and delayed characterization does not establish immediate post-irradiation performance or in-orbit recovery.
infographic.paper_title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells

title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yezeyuan Zheng, Ziyang Hu, Maojun Sun. Ruijian Han, Jian Huang, Guanhua Chen, Jie Liu
abstract: Experimental optimization of perovskite solar cells is constrained by combinatorial diversity in absorber compositions, device layers, and processing, which makes virtual screening attractive for prioritizing recipes before fabrication. We develop a surrogate-guided reinforcement-learning framework that casts recipe generation as virtual screening, enriching candidate shortlists near high-performing experimental neighbors. A frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) guides recipe generation, while a reference pool of 890 measured devices enables neighborhood-based assessment. Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices shows top-ten selection raises mean power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 19.68\% to 23.74\%. Three learned policies are compared with six baselines under 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run. In top-100 shortlists, Proximal policy optimization (PPO) and recurrent PPO (RPPO) achieve neighborhood-supported hit rates of 23\% and 24\% (7.9- and 8.3-fold Pure Random's 2.9\%), versus 10\% (3.4-fold) for the baselines with the highest supported hit rate (L-SHADE and Ax BO, tied) at $K = 100$. Gains coexist with weak-support fractions. Of 9,000 recipes, 65.4\% match a composition family at similarity 0.80, falling to 11.7\% at 0.90. Results support enrichment-oriented prioritization but not experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.

infographic.key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches virtual perovskite recipe shortlists for candidates near high-performing measured devices.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize perovskite compositions, device layers, and processing recipes before costly fabrication.
method: Generate device recipes using reinforcement-learning policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support against 890 measured reference devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
infographic.evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates were 23–24% for PPO/RPPO versus 2.9% for random sampling and 10% for the strongest baselines.
infographic.watch_item: Neighborhood enrichment does not establish experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage; composition-family coverage also falls sharply at stricter similarity thresholds.
infographic.paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
authors: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo
abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal-cycling damage.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Engineering interfacial adhesion offers a route to reduce stress-driven failure during temperature fluctuations relevant to photovoltaic deployment.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl species to enable multipoint anchoring dominated by metal–oxygen coordination.
Use cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to reinforce interfacial anchoring.
infographic.evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85 °C under ISOS-T-3.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether these gains persist in large-area modules or under combined outdoor stressors.
infographic.paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells

title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Ying Tang, Zuhong Zhang, Hongzhuo Wu, Zhihao Li, Zhenhuang Su, Yonggang Yang
abstract: Tin-based perovskites are promising candidates for lead-free photovoltaics but suffer from labile Sn$^{2+}$ coordination, rapid crystallization, and severe interfacial defects. Here, we develop a dynamic molecular transformation using 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) to regulate crystallization and interface chemistry simultaneously. During nucleation and growth, the carbonyl group coordinates with Sn$^{2+}$ to stabilize precursor complexes, moderate supersaturation, and enable controlled crystal growth. Upon annealing, PX undergoes in situ molecular transformation, suggested to form amidinium-functionalized species that preferentially occupy surface A-site vacancies, forming a passivation layer and suppressing nonradiative recombination. This coupled bulk-to-interface evolution yields compact, highly crystalline films with improved optoelectronic quality. Devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.18% and retain 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 h of continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a dynamic molecular engineering approach integrating crystallization control and interface passivation, providing a pathway toward efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: A dynamically transforming 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) additive couples crystallization control with interface passivation in lead-free tin-based perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This molecular engineering approach targets both film formation and interfacial defects to improve photovoltaic efficiency and operational stability.
method: Coordinate PX carbonyl groups with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and regulate crystal growth.
Anneal films to induce PX transformation, suggested to produce amidinium-functionalized species.
Passivate surface A-site vacancies to suppress nonradiative recombination.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retention of 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
infographic.watch_item: The proposed amidinium-forming transformation remains tentative, and the abstract does not specify illumination-test conditions or device-scale reproducibility.
infographic.paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells

title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery
authors: Yingheng Wang, Francesco Ricci, Zhilong Wang, Tao Yu, Junwen Bai, Xiangyun Lei
abstract: Predicting a material's behavior from its atomic structure is a longstanding goal of the physical sciences. The electronic and phonon densities of states (eDOS and phDOS) govern key electronic, optical, vibrational, and thermodynamic properties, yet their calculation using density functional theory (DFT) is costly: about 60% of Materials Project entries lack eDOS and over 80% lack phDOS. Existing crystal-to-spectrum models rely on pooled structural representations and pointwise regression, which blur spectral features and violate total-state conservation. Here we introduce DeepDOSReasoner, a physics-grounded framework that decodes spectra through atom-to-energy source attention and refines the normalized DOS through learned continuity-equation transport, enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation by construction. DeepDOSReasoner achieves the highest prediction accuracy across all evaluated metrics for both eDOS and phDOS, recovers element-resolved contributions without supervision, and most reliably identifies rare valence-band (VB) gaps. In a prospective screen of 8,106 uncharted materials validated by new DFT calculations, its predictions remain the most accurate among the methods evaluated, with 25 of its top 50 candidates confirmed as VB-gap materials. Three case studies spanning substituted compounds, photovoltaic chalcogenides, and a high-entropy alloy demonstrate transfer across materials classes. Ablations confirm that both stages are necessary, while the model retains comparable accuracy when trained on only 25% of the data. Predicting spectra in milliseconds enables exhaustive screening; we release predictions filling the missing eDOS for 91,405 and phDOS for 127,768 Materials Project entries. DeepDOSReasoner provides a blueprint for integrating machine learning with physical reasoning toward high-throughput spectral screening and autonomous materials discovery.

infographic.key_insight: DeepDOSReasoner predicts electronic and phonon density-of-states spectra from crystal structures while enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Millisecond-scale spectral predictions could accelerate materials screening, including photovoltaic chalcogenides, but do not directly predict solar-cell efficiency.
method: Decode spectra using atom-to-energy source attention.
Refine normalized spectra through learned continuity-equation transport.
Preserve nonnegativity and total spectral weight by construction.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports best accuracy across evaluated metrics and a prospective screen of 8,106 materials, with new DFT calculations confirming valence-band gaps in 25 of the model’s top 50 candidates.
infographic.watch_item: DFT-validated spectral accuracy and valence-band-gap discovery do not establish experimental photovoltaic performance.
infographic.paper_title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery

title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
authors: Zhaoheng Ling, Linqu Luo, Chrysa Aivalioti, Temur Maksudov, Mengxi Zhang, Theodoulos Kalogerakis
abstract: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

infographic.key_insight: Selenium alloying and air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% peak efficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improve oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers made by scalable vacuum deposition.
method: Thermally evaporate a 90:10 wt% TeO2:Se powder mixture.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours to tune composition and defects.
Integrate an 80 nm absorber into an ITO/ZnO/TeOx:Se/MoOx/Ag solar cell.
infographic.evidence_signal: Optimized 9-hour-annealed devices delivered 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, 0.44 fill factor, and photocurrent response from 300–1000 nm; film analysis found approximately 0.4% residual metallic Te.
infographic.watch_item: The 9-hour anneal may constrain manufacturing throughput, and the abstract does not establish long-term device stability.
infographic.paper_title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells

title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
authors: Nabanita Sarker, Hafiz Imtiaz
abstract: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.

infographic.key_insight: Machine learning can identify simulated degradation mechanisms in lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but reliable prediction depends strongly on training-data coverage.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Temperature- and illumination-dependent voltage measurements could support post-fabrication diagnosis, while replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor gains.
method: Generate approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D device simulations.
Compare forward surrogate models trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Use a multi-label classifier to detect six degradation mechanisms from open-circuit-voltage measurements.
infographic.evidence_signal: Diagnostic macro F1 reaches 0.938 versus 0.687 for calibrated physics rules; forward-model R² falls from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, recovering to 0.995 with Latin hypercube training.
infographic.watch_item: Diagnosis is demonstrated on simulated data and fails to generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training.
infographic.paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements

title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
authors: Jan-Frederik Pietschmann, Carmen Tretmans, Nicola Zamponi
abstract: We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.

infographic.key_insight: A thermodynamically consistent phase-field model couples donor–acceptor phase separation, solvent evaporation, and fluid flow during organic solar-cell active-layer formation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could support simulations linking drying and fluid motion to active-layer morphology in organic photovoltaic manufacturing.
method: Couple incompressible Navier–Stokes, multispecies Cahn–Hilliard, and Allen–Cahn equations.
Include degenerate mobility and cross-diffusion terms.
Prove global-in-time weak-solution existence and total-energy dissipation.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical existence and energy-dissipation results without size constraints on the data, but no experimental validation or numerical benchmarks.
infographic.watch_item: Degenerate mobility requires a specialized variational definition of diffusion fluxes, which may complicate numerical implementation.
infographic.paper_title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells

title: Giant magnetic anisotropy in layered polar metal Sr$_3$Co$_2$O$_7$ from Charge-disproportionation orbital unquenching
authors: Houssam Sabri, Hong-Fei Huang, Jie-Xiang Yu, Jiadong Zang
abstract: Crystal-field quenching usually suppresses orbital angular momentum and limits magnetic anisotropy in transition-metal oxides. Here we identify charge disproportionation as a route to giant magnetocrystalline anisotropy in the layered polar metal Sr$_3$Co$_2$O$_7$. First-principles calculations reveal an energy preference of 234.0 meV per cell for in-plane [110] magnetization over [001]. Charge disproportionation and the associated polar displacement reconstruct the local cobalt crystal fields, creating inequivalent sites with distinct orbital hierarchies. This reconstruction enables a strongly directional orbital response, particularly at the displaced cobalt site, where orbital angular momentum is recovered for in-plane magnetization. Spin--orbit coupling converts this response into a large magnetic anisotropic energy. In the centrosymmetric reference, the orbital moments remain nearly quenched and the anisotropy is strongly reduced. A local Green-function and orbital-moment analysis connects the large energy scale to orbital unquenching, while the conventional second-order contribution is small within the adopted approximation. These results identify charge-disproportionation-driven orbital reconstruction as a design principle for large anisotropy and motivate layered perovskites and magnetic polar metals as platforms in the search for rare-earth-free permanent magnets.

infographic.key_insight: Charge disproportionation restores directional cobalt orbital angular momentum in layered polar metal Sr₃Co₂O₇, producing giant magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The proposed mechanism could guide rare-earth-free permanent-magnet design; this paper concerns magnetic materials, not AI or solar cells.
method: First-principles calculations of magnetization-direction-dependent energies.
Comparison of polar and centrosymmetric structures.
Local Green-function and orbital-moment analysis.
infographic.evidence_signal: Calculations favor in-plane [110] magnetization over [001] by 234.0 meV per cell, while the centrosymmetric reference shows nearly quenched orbital moments and strongly reduced anisotropy.
infographic.watch_item: The computational result requires experimental validation, and large anisotropy alone does not establish permanent-magnet performance.
infographic.paper_title: Giant magnetic anisotropy in layered polar metal Sr$_3$Co$_2$O$_7$ from Charge-disproportionation orbital unquenching

title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
authors: Mahmoud Samadpour, Alireza Fathi Beiraghvandi, Kazem Meraji, Tristan Sachsenweger Ballantyne, Fuxiang Ji, Mahdi Mohammadi
abstract: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving photoluminescence and preserving electronic uniformity, even under accelerated aging.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Surface smoothness alone may be an unreliable quality metric when designing durable perovskite solar cells.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Combine statistical AFM topography analysis with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare capped and pristine films for emission and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
infographic.evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting than pristine films.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports film-level results without quantitative effect sizes or device-level efficiency and operational-lifetime validation.
infographic.paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures

title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
authors: Mahesh Eledath-Changarath, Jesús Ortiga-Fibla, Andrés F. Gualdrón-Reyes, Jesús Rodríguez-Romero, Iván Mora-Seró, Ana Cros
abstract: Long-term stability remains a critical challenge limiting the photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites. In these materials, the choice of the organic spacer plays a key role not only in enhancing environmental stability, but also in determining their structural characteristics and carrier dynamics. Here, we present an environmental photo- and thermal-stability analysis of BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 two-dimensional lead halide perovskites by means of confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy techniques. We have investigated two different organic spacers, n-butylammonium (BA) and 2-phenylethylammonium (PEA), which provide comparable room-temperature luminescence in freshly exfoliated perovskite nanoflakes and degrade similarly through the removal of organic components and fast crystal phase decomposition into PbI2 and Pb0. However, we observed that the PEA organic cation significantly improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, resulting in slower degradation and enhanced resistance to light and thermal stress under ambient conditions. Our findings indicate that structural and chemical engineering, along with surface passivation and encapsulation strategies, are essential for achieving long-term stability in two-dimensional halide perovskite devices. Nevertheless, optimizing the balance between stability and device performance remains a critical consideration.

infographic.key_insight: PEA spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskites under ambient light and thermal stress.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to assess degradation.
Examined morphology, lattice defects, and luminescence in exfoliated nanoflakes.
infographic.evidence_signal: Fresh nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or operational lifetime, so device-level stability–performance trade-offs remain unresolved.
infographic.paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites

title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods
authors: Julian Ruddick
abstract: The transition from fossil fuels presents significant challenges in energy management. To ensure a sustainable energy future, it is crucial to reduce energy consumption when possible and to synchronize electricity consumption and storage with the production from sources with low greenhouse gas emissions. This thesis explores a variety of energy management methods used to manage batteries, heat pumps, and other energy-related systems. The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases. The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. However, on average, these cost savings do not yet outweigh the current costs and effort required to implement such algorithms.

infographic.key_insight: TreeC learns understandable residential energy-management strategies with competitive performance against model predictive control and reinforcement learning.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Coordinating batteries, heat pumps, EV charging, and photovoltaic systems can reduce electricity costs, though implementation costs may outweigh savings.
method: Compare rule-based, optimization, and machine-learning energy management.
Develop TreeC to learn understandable control strategies.
Evaluate methods in three simulation cases and one real-world experiment.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive TreeC performance across diverse problems, but both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse on real hardware than in simulations.
infographic.watch_item: Deployment requires representative training data and reliable real-time inputs; current implementation costs and effort exceed average savings in the studied Belgian dwellings.
infographic.paper_title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods

title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
authors: Shiling Dong, Yongjie Wang, Hae-Jun Seok, Mengyuan Huang, Edward Newton, Der Ying Chen
abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.5% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

infographic.key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers, supporting 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with lead-halide perovskite sub-cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Improved carrier extraction in thicker AgBiS2 films offers a route to scalable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange for one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with perovskite sub-cells in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies >47.5% are modeled, not demonstrated.
infographic.watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
infographic.paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics

title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production
authors: Ivana Staničić, Alfred Juhlin Onbeck, Anders Hellman, Tobias Mattisson, Magnus Rydén
abstract: Perovskites are promising materials for chemical looping hydrogen production (CLHP) due to their compositional flexibility and tunable redox properties. However, cation substitution opens a vast compositional space, making screening for new high-performing materials computationally demanding. Here, an autonomous active-learning framework combining a Wasserstein autoencoder (WAE) with a deep ensemble surrogate model was used to search for perovskites with a high hydrogen production capacity (HPC). In seven independent runs of 50 cycles, the mean HPC of the acquired compositions rose from 0.41 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$ in the starting set to 2.05 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$, and the best compositions reached 2.65-2.99 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$. All runs enriched Sn on the B-site, mostly combined with Ti and with Mg, Ce, K and Y on the A-site. Twenty diverse candidates (2.22-2.84 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$) were then selected by a multi-objective ranking that also accounts for raw-material price, supply resilience and potential environmental and health impacts. The approach links materials discovery with practical deployment constraints, and the methodology is transferable to other chemical looping processes.

infographic.key_insight: An autonomous AI workflow identified perovskite compositions with high predicted hydrogen production capacity for chemical looping, rather than solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Combining hydrogen capacity with raw-material price, supply resilience, and potential environmental and health impacts helps prioritize candidates for practical deployment.
method: Combine a Wasserstein autoencoder with a deep ensemble surrogate in an active-learning loop.
Search perovskite compositions for high hydrogen production capacity.
Use multi-objective ranking to select 20 diverse candidates.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across seven independent 50-cycle runs, mean acquired hydrogen capacity rose from 0.41 to 2.05 mmol H₂/g, with best compositions reaching 2.65–2.99 mmol H₂/g.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not report experimental validation or long-term redox cycling stability, both essential before deployment.
infographic.paper_title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production

title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
authors: Arash Omidi, Tanmay Mishra, Mads R. Almassalkhi
abstract: This paper presents a constraint-aware reinforcement learning (CARL) controller for battery energy storage system (BESS) sizing and photovoltaic (PV) ramp-rate smoothing. Rapid PV power fluctuations caused by cloud transitions can introduce operational and stability challenges in power systems. To mitigate these impacts, grid codes impose ramp-rate limits (RRL) on PV power injected to the grid. BESSs can support such grid codes by absorbing or supplying power during rapid variations. However, the extent to which BESSs can reduce PV-induced variability depends on (i) the BESS power and energy capacities; and (ii) the adopted controller. Thus, BESS sizing and controller design are coupled. Conventional moving-average control can increase battery usage due to filter-induced lag, while ramp-rate control is reactive and does not account for the long-term impact of actions on battery state of charge and future ramp events. Optimization-based methods can reduce BESS requirements by anticipating future PV variations, but their performance depends on accurate PV forecasts. To address these limitations, the CARL controller learns a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment. Ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints are incorporated into a causal feasibility interval that guarantees feasible actions by definition. A full-horizon input-convex neural network (ICNN)-based optimization is developed as a noncausal benchmark for the minimum achievable BESS requirements. Evaluation using three real-world PV datasets shows that, at a 10\%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduces peak BESS power by 8.7--10.4\% and energy capacity by 47.5--62.6\% relative to conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining the grid-codes compliance.

infographic.key_insight: Constraint-aware reinforcement learning reduces battery sizing needs for PV ramp-rate smoothing while maintaining grid-code compliance.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Jointly designing battery capacity and control can reduce storage requirements for integrating variable solar generation into the grid.
method: Learn a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment.
Restrict battery actions to a feasibility interval incorporating ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints.
Use full-horizon input-convex neural network optimization as a noncausal benchmark for minimum battery requirements.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across three real-world PV datasets at a 10%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduced peak battery power by 8.7–10.4% and energy capacity by 47.5–62.6% versus conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining compliance.
infographic.watch_item: Generalization to unseen PV variability and real-world battery behavior requires further validation beyond the reported datasets.
infographic.paper_title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller

title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
authors: Cristóbal Méndez, Justin Tahmassebpur, Tomás A. Arias
abstract: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. In a search for phonon-mediated superconductors, density-functional perturbation theory on 45 structurally novel designs gives isotropic Allen-Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39; the highest is 24.0 K for ZrTiNb2CN3, and H4LiPd3 (23.2 K) lies on the static DFT hull. In searches for photovoltaic absorbers, SCAN calculations confirm ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull, and show that the systematic gap error of the training functional propagates into the designs unless the objective corrects for it. Quasiharmonic free energies from machine-learned potentials further show that finite-temperature competition with solid phases can reorder candidates relative to the static hull.

infographic.key_insight: DEFEAT enables gradient-based crystal design by jointly optimizing composition and structure, including candidate semiconductors with band gaps targeted for solar absorption.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate photovoltaic absorber discovery by searching elemental choices, atom counts, positions, and lattice geometry together.
method: Extend pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data.
Optimize crystals using gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty.
Validate candidate band gaps and stability with SCAN calculations and assess finite-temperature phase competition.
infographic.evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirmed ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
infographic.watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; target gaps alone do not establish solar-cell performance.
infographic.paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models

title: Power Law Transients in Perovskite Photoluminescence
authors: Anas M. M., Pradeep R. Nair
abstract: Carrier dynamics and recombination in perovskite thin films are often explored through transient photoluminescence (PL) measurements and subsequent analysis based on single/multi-exponentials. In contrast, here we show that several experimental PL transients reported in literature vary as power laws with time and are not multi-exponentials. Puzzlingly, the existing theoretical methods are ill-equipped to explain the origin and implications of such power law trends. Our analysis resolves this puzzle and correlates the power law exponents with the trap distributions. Curiously, we show that PL transients could vary as $t^{-2}$ even in the presence of dominant monomolecular recombination while the existing theory associates this unique trend exclusively with dominant bimolecular recombination. These findings identify the limits of applicability of concepts such as differential lifetime and highlight the need for predictive modeling synergistic with insightful data analysis towards performance optimization of perovskite optoelectronic devices.

infographic.key_insight: Power-law photoluminescence decays reveal trap distributions, and a t⁻² decay can occur even when monomolecular—not bimolecular—recombination dominates.
infographic.engineering_relevance: More accurate interpretation of photoluminescence transients can guide defect characterization and performance optimization in perovskite solar cells.
method: Analyze experimental photoluminescence transients reported in the literature.
Relate power-law decay exponents to trap distributions.
Examine recombination regimes and limits of differential-lifetime interpretation.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports power-law behavior in several published experimental transients but provides no dataset sizes or quantitative fit comparisons.
infographic.watch_item: Do not infer the dominant recombination mechanism from a t⁻² decay alone; the abstract describes no AI method.
infographic.paper_title: Power Law Transients in Perovskite Photoluminescence
